risk: Two Adults can turn the call into an information dump or a technical debate, and jargon can creep in unchecked.
relateStrategy: Match their precision. Lead with the answer, then the evidence. Cite the exact policy and timeline, then invite questions.
phrasesToUse: Short answer: yes, by Thursday. Here's why.
Which detail would you like me to walk through?

risk: Cold logic (Adult) alienates the emotional customer (Adapted Child). Facts before validation create a crossed transaction.
relateStrategy: Force empathy before logic. Validate the emotion first.
phrasesToUse: I realize this whole thing has been frustrating for you.

risk: Correcting a Critical Parent with facts sounds like "you're wrong" and starts a battle of egos over who is right.
relateStrategy: Acknowledge the principle and their loyalty first. Then present the facts as the plan, not as a rebuttal.
phrasesToUse: You've been with us a long time. You're right to expect better.
Here's what we know. Here's what we've done. Here's what's next.

risk: Laying out every option with pros and cons overloads a risk-averse customer and causes analysis paralysis.
relateStrategy: Narrow to two options, recommend one with a single clear reason, and reassure them it can be changed.
phrasesToUse: Based on what you've told me, I'd recommend this one because...
If it doesn't suit you, we can change it later.
phrasesToAvoid: There are several options. Let me go through all of them.

risk: Fact-only delivery feels cold to a rapport-seeker, who then talks more to get a connection.
relateStrategy: Offer a moment of genuine warmth, then channel their energy into short, simple steps.
phrasesToUse: That sounds like quite a week. Let's make this the easy part of it.
Here's the quick version, three steps.

risk: Low risk. Over-explaining to someone who already understands wastes their time.
relateStrategy: Stay efficient. Confirm understanding and next steps, and thank them for their help.
phrasesToUse: Thanks, that saves us time. Here's what happens next.
Anything else I can clear up while I have you?

risk: Emotional mirroring reads as filler, or even as patronizing, to someone who only wants accurate answers.
relateStrategy: Tone down emotional language. Show care through accuracy, precision, and follow-through.
phrasesToUse: Here are the exact details.
I'll confirm this in writing so you have the reference number.
phrasesToAvoid: Oh no, I'm so sorry you're going through this!
I totally understand how you feel.

risk: Over-nurturing keeps the customer in the Child state and lengthens the call, and the agent absorbs the distress.
relateStrategy: Validate briefly, then give structured steps that move the customer toward Adult. Keep care separate from absorbing their stress.
phrasesToUse: I'm going to take care of this with you. First, ...
Other customers have felt the same way, and here's what worked.

risk: May fold under Critical Parent pressure, over-apologizing and losing institutional authority.
relateStrategy: Shift consciously to the Adult state. Assert boundaries with structure.
phrasesToUse: Here's what we know. Here's what we've done. Here's what's next.

risk: Endless reassurance without a recommendation keeps the customer undecided and the call drags on.
relateStrategy: Reassure, then recommend clearly. A gentle directive helps them decide.
phrasesToUse: What I suggest is...
Many customers in your situation choose this, and it's easy to change later.
phrasesToAvoid: Take all the time you need.

risk: Mutual warmth turns into a long social call and handle time balloons.
relateStrategy: Enjoy the connection, but set the agenda early and use friendly bridges back to the task.
phrasesToUse: I love that. Let me get this sorted for you while we chat.
Before I forget, let me confirm one detail.

risk: Low risk. Over-apologizing to a customer who doesn't need it.
relateStrategy: Stay warm and efficient. Confirm the outcome and show appreciation.
phrasesToUse: Thank you for having that ready. That makes this quick.

risk: Casual, conversational tone reads as unprofessional or untrustworthy to a customer who wants precision.
relateStrategy: Drop conversational filler. Speak in exact numbers, metrics, and policies. Outline precise timelines.
phrasesToUse: I will make sure this gets resolved by taking [X] steps.
phrasesToAvoid: Let me try to fix this.

risk: A casual tone or humor minimizes the worry of a customer who is anxious.
relateStrategy: Set the jokes aside and slow down. Use calm, plain language and take visible ownership.
phrasesToUse: I hear you. I'm going to stay with you until this is sorted.
Here's the first thing we'll do.

risk: Informality reads as not taking them seriously, and the customer asks for a manager.
relateStrategy: Make your tone more formal and use their name. State clear commitments and take ownership of them.
phrasesToUse: [Name], I'm taking ownership of this.
Here's exactly what I'm going to do, and by when.
phrasesToAvoid: I'll see what I can do.

risk: Friendly but non-directive ("up to you!") leaves the customer without the guidance they need.
relateStrategy: Use the rapport to build trust, then recommend the way a trusted friend would.
phrasesToUse: If I were in your shoes, I'd go with...
Are you able to try this first? If it doesn't work, we'll switch.

risk: You both love to chat, so handle time balloons and the resolution gets lost.
relateStrategy: Enjoy the rapport but keep steering. Set a light agenda and summarize before closing.
phrasesToUse: Okay, let's get you sorted so you can get back to it.
Quick recap before I let you go...

risk: Low risk. An easy, casual flow can skip required verification or recap steps.
relateStrategy: Keep the easy flow but still complete every verification, disclosure, and recap.
phrasesToUse: Perfect. I just need to confirm a couple of details for security.
phrasesToAvoid: Skipping the recap because the call is going well

risk: Speed can skip the explanation, and the Analytical customer won't agree until they understand why.
relateStrategy: Give the plan and the reasoning together. Provide reference numbers and exact timelines.
phrasesToUse: Here's the plan, and here's why it works.
Your reference number is [X]. You'll see the update by [date].
phrasesToAvoid: Just trust me, this will fix it.

risk: Rushing to resolution leaves the customer feeling unheard, so the anxiety rises.
relateStrategy: Slow down for the first 30 seconds: listen fully, restate, validate. Then lead one step at a time.
phrasesToUse: So you're worried because [restate]. Is that right?
We'll do this one step at a time.

risk: Two directive styles collide into a power struggle, and a blunt refusal sounds like a challenge.
relateStrategy: Stay in Adult, not Critical Parent. Acknowledge the principle, then use assertive optioning.
phrasesToUse: While I can't do X, what I can do right now is Y.
Here's what we know. Here's what we've done. Here's what's next.

risk: The drive for immediate resolution overwhelms the customer, who freezes or abandons the call.
relateStrategy: Use assertive optioning and gentle, collaborative questions.
phrasesToUse: Are you able to...?
What I suggest is...
phrasesToAvoid: I need you to give me your serial number now.

risk: Cutting off stories feels dismissive, and the customer disengages or pushes back.
relateStrategy: Give a brief, warm acknowledgement, then redirect with energy toward a quick win.
phrasesToUse: That's great. Let's get this done so you can get back to it.
Here's the fastest way to fix this.
phrasesToAvoid: Can we get back on topic?

risk: Low risk. The call can feel purely transactional and miss a chance to build loyalty.
relateStrategy: Resolve efficiently and add a brief personal close.
phrasesToUse: Done. You're all set. Thanks for making that easy.
phrasesToAvoid: Ending abruptly without confirming everything is resolved

risk: Workarounds with no documented basis erode trust with a customer who expects strict policy adherence.
relateStrategy: Anchor any creative solution in policy and documentation, and explain exactly how it works.
phrasesToUse: This option is covered under [policy]. Here's how it works, step by step.
I'll send you written confirmation of this.
phrasesToAvoid: Let's try something different and see what happens.
I'm not sure it's official, but...

risk: Too many ideas and pivots feel chaotic and add to the anxiety.
relateStrategy: Pick one solution and present it calmly and simply. Keep the creativity behind the scenes.
phrasesToUse: I've got a solution for this. Here's the first step.
I'll handle the details on my end.
phrasesToAvoid: We could try this, or maybe this, or...

risk: Unstructured, rule-bending approach violates the customer's need for order and perceived justice.
relateStrategy: Frame the workaround as a special exception honoring their loyalty. State it firmly.
phrasesToUse: I can give you a $50 credit.
phrasesToAvoid: The most I can offer is...

risk: Unfamiliar options raise the perceived risk and the customer stalls.
relateStrategy: Lead with the proven path. Frame any alternative as safe and reversible.
phrasesToUse: Most customers go with this, and it works well.
This is easy to undo if you change your mind.
phrasesToAvoid: Here's a creative option nobody usually tries.
Offering a long list of alternatives

risk: Shared energy and tangents make the call long and unfocused, and it's easy to over-promise.
relateStrategy: Enjoy the energy, then commit to one idea and confirm exactly what's promised.
phrasesToUse: Love it. Here's what I'll lock in for you today.
phrasesToAvoid: We could maybe do all of that!

risk: Low risk. May overcomplicate a simple request.
relateStrategy: Solve the stated need first. Offer extras only if they're relevant.
phrasesToUse: Here's the simplest fix. Want me to also set up [X] so this doesn't happen again?
phrasesToAvoid: Unrequested workarounds for a simple request

risk: Diplomatic hedging and softeners read as evasive or vague.
relateStrategy: Be direct and precise. Keep the tact, but state facts plainly.
phrasesToUse: The answer is no for X and yes for Y. Here's why.
The exact timeline is [X].
phrasesToAvoid: We'll see what we can do.

risk: Deep acting drains the agent, who may start mirroring the customer's anxiety.
relateStrategy: Validate, normalize, then move into structure. Take a short reset after the call.
phrasesToUse: I get how you feel. Other customers have felt the same, and here's what worked.
Let's take this one step at a time.

risk: Constant accommodation looks like weakness, so the customer pushes for more and the agent wears out.
relateStrategy: Acknowledge, then hold firm boundaries with calm structure. Offer options, not concessions.
phrasesToUse: I understand why this matters to you. Here's what I can do.
While I can't do X, what I can do is Y.
phrasesToAvoid: I'll see if maybe I can...
Conceding just to end the pressure

risk: Being too balanced: presenting everything evenly and never making a recommendation.
relateStrategy: Use the rapport to guide them, and make the recommendation explicit.
phrasesToUse: Weighing what you've told me, I'd recommend...
Are you comfortable going ahead with that?
phrasesToAvoid: Both are good options. It's really up to you.

risk: Tangential stories derail the call and inflate Average Handle Time.
relateStrategy: Acknowledge the story warmly (Nurturing Parent), then pivot to the task (Adult).
phrasesToUse: That sounds like a great trip. Let's get this account secured so you can enjoy the rest of it.

risk: Low risk. Unneeded smoothing lengthens an easy call.
relateStrategy: Be efficient and save your energy for the harder calls.
phrasesToUse: Great, we're on the same page. Here's what happens next.
